To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the mRNA expression pattern for the matrix metallopeptidases MT1-MMP gelatinase A (MMP2), and the glycoproteins EMMPRIN (CD147) was studied using in situ mRNA hybridization on 35S-labled antisense and sense probes in formalin fixed paraffin-embeded breast tissue from 18 patients with invasive breast carcinoma.

the mRNA expression for gelatinases A, MT1-matrix metallopeptidase, and EMMPRII was seen in invasive breast carcinomas, but no differences in expression were seen in patients that survived compared to those who died from metastasis.

gelatinase A expression is mainly localized to stromally infiltrating tumor cells, and that the expression of gelatinase-A, MT1-MPP, and EMMP-RIN mRNA are correlated with the invasive phenotype of the carcinoma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the extracellular matrix metal-loproteinase inducer, EMMPRIN, as an important regulator of the invasive phenotype in human breast carcinoma.
the development of new therapeutic approaches in breast cancer.
the role of gelatinase, MT1-MP, and EMMPRI in breast carcinoma and the correlation between mRNA expression of these proteins in the invasive phenotype.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
gelatinase A expression is a marker for invasive growth in breast cancer and that MT1-MMP may be a marker for aggressive tumor behavior in breast cancer.
the gelatinase A-MT1-MMP-EMMPRIN pathway is a central pathway in the invasive phenotype in the majority of human breast carcinomas.
EMMPRIN, MT1-MPP, and gelatinase A are important for the aggressive phenotype in breast cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
gelatinase A expression is mainly localized to stromatocytes, whereas EMMPRIN and MT1-MP mRNA is localized to the tumor cells in invasive breast carcinoma.
the expression of gelatinase, MT1-MPP, and EMMP-RIN in breast carcinoma is not associated with a poor clinical outcome.
EMMPRIN and MT1-MP may be important for the invasive growth of breast cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
gelatinase A expression is not a good prognostic factor in breast carcinoma, and that EMMPRIN expression is not correlated with survival in this study.
the mRNA expression pattern is not related to the outcome of the disease.
EMMPRIN, gelatinase-A and MT1-MPP may be useful targets for breast cancer treatment.
